⚡️ Iranian Armed Forces chief pledges full support for IRGC

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Chief of Staff of the Iranian Armed Forces Major General Ali Abdollahi has congratulated Major General Ahmad Vahidi on his appointment as commander-in-chief of the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC), stressing the Armed Forces General Staff’s full readiness to provide strategic support to the IRGC.

In a message congratulating Vahidi on his appointment and promotion to the rank of major general, Abdollahi said on Tuesday that the decision by the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei, reflected Vahidi’s capabilities, competence and outstanding qualifications.
​
He described the appointment as a strategic step toward consolidating sustainable security and further strengthening the Islamic Republic of Iran.
​
Abdollahi also commended the IRGC’s longstanding role in defending the Islamic Revolution and contributing to the country’s defense, security and development, and emphasized the Armed Forces General Staff’s readiness to provide comprehensive support and strategic assistance to the IRGC.
​
He said the General Staff would mobilize its capacities to strengthen the IRGC’s defense and security capabilities in response to emerging regional and extra-regional threats, modernize its equipment, systems and operational structures, and ensure the timely provision of its operational requirements.
​
These efforts would cover key areas including missile and drone capabilities, naval and ground operations, cyberspace and asymmetric warfare, he added.
​
Abdollahi further stressed the need to enhance coordination among the different branches of the Armed Forces to maximize Iran’s defense capabilities and strengthen the Basij as a broad-based popular force.
​
He said greater unity, coordination, and strategic cooperation among the Armed Forces would help reinforce Iran’s deterrent power and strengthen its ability to confront threats and hostile plots.
​
Abdollahi wished Vahidi and the commanders and personnel of the IRGC continued success, stressing the importance of following the directives and guidance of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution and Commander-in-Chief of the Iranian Armed Forces, Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei.

Crypto Idea

Long-Term investing strategy

When the crypto market is falling, buying feels scary. When it's going up, it feels like you've already missed your chance.

As a result, most people either buy based on emotion or keep waiting for the perfect entry point — and end up doing nothing at all.

But there's a simple way to avoid this problem: invest a fixed amount of money at regular intervals.

This strategy is called DCA (Dollar-Cost Averaging).

You simply choose the asset, the amount you want to invest, and how often you want to buy.

For example:
$50 worth of Bitcoin every week.

When Bitcoin is cheaper, your $50 buys more. When it's more expensive, it buys less. Over time, your average purchase price naturally evens out, and over the course of a few years, it often ends up being better than the average market participant's.

Bybit even has a built-in Auto-Invest bot designed specifically for this strategy. You set it up once — choose your currency, the coin, the investment amount, and the schedule.

After that, your purchases happen automatically, whether it's every day or once a month. The key is to choose a coin you genuinely believe in for the long term.

📌 Rollup Sequencers: The Gatekeepers of Layer 2 Blocks

Main Points
⏺ Sequencers order transactions on Layer 2 and send batches to the base chain
⏺ They control UX: speed, ordering, and sometimes fees
⏺ This post explains why sequencers are crucial for rollups — and why decentralizing them matters

1️⃣ Role — sequencers receive user transactions, decide their order, and produce L2 blocks or batches.
2️⃣ Fast UX — they can give near-instant confirmations on L2 while final settlement still happens on L1.
3️⃣ Centralization Risk — many rollups start with a single sequencer, which can censor or reorder transactions.
4️⃣ MEV & Fairness — who controls ordering also touches MEV, so sequencer design affects how value is captured or shared.
5️⃣ Roadmap — serious rollups work toward decentralized or shared-sequencer models to reduce trust assumptions.

Final Thoughts

Sequencers are the “traffic controllers” of rollups — invisible to most users, but central to how fair, fast, and decentralized Layer 2 really is.
